title: AlphaFold model of full-length honey bee vitellogenin restrained by electron microscopy
summary: Researchers modeled full-length honey bee vitellogenin using homology modeling and AlphaFold, then used a negative-stain electron microscopy map to restrain, orient and validate the model. The model identified a highly conserved Ca2+-binding site in a von Willebrand factor domain that may be central to Vg function, and the authors describe it as the first experimentally validated full-length Vg protein model. The EM map is low resolution and the Ca2+ site is predicted, not measured.
ai_technology: AlphaFold and homology modeling of full-length vitellogenin

evidence.tested: Structure prediction restrained and checked against a negative-stain EM map.
evidence.unknown: Ca2+-binding site is a prediction not tested biochemically; EM resolution is low; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold and homology modeling predicted domain structures that were assembled into a full-length model.
